questions.statement:
The European Island That Swaps Nationality Twice a Year
Sophie-May Williams
01
“There are no pheasants __ Pheasant Island,” complained the French author Victor Hugo
02 __ 1843. Calm down, Mr. Hugo. The lack __ game birds is the least interesting thing __ the
03 place. Less than 200 meters long and 40 meters wide, this tiny stretch of land on the Bidasoa
04 River between France and Spain boasts something truly unique: it changes nationality every six
05 months.
06
Let’s backtrack a bit. Pheasant Island is uninhabited, briefly home to migratory birds and
07 wild animals, and lush with greenery. Sunshine is permanent, thanks to the year-long subtropical
08 climate. The only structure is a 19th-century monolith that shares both Spanish and French
09 inscriptions, a symbol of peace between the two nations. But there’s more to this geopolitical
10 anomaly than meets the eye. From February 1 to July 31, it’s under Spanish rule. Then, from
11 August 1 to January 31, it belongs to France.
12
Despite adhering to such a curious concept, few people have heard of the island. Or what
13 it stands for. Back in 1659, it served as the signing location for the Treaty of the Pyrenees. This
14 was a significant peace treaty between Louis XIV of France and Philip IV of Spain, as it ended
15 the 30-year Franco-Spanish War. Remember the tomb-like monolith from earlier? It was erected
16 centuries later to commemorate this very meeting. In simple terms, it gave each nation the
17 chance to govern the humanless island. Sharing is caring, after all. The occasion was so
18 momentous that a year later, French King Louis XIV married the daughter of King Philip IV, Maria
19 Theresa of Spain, in the exact spot where the treaty was signed. Wooden bridges were erected
20 so royal entourages could pass through in barges and carriages, and paintings were
21 commissioned to immortalize the event.
22
These days, general access to Pheasant Island is prohibited. The only time you might be

In the sentence “Few people have heard of the island” (l. 12), what does the phrasal verb “heard of” mean?

options.text: Listened carefully to something.
Been warned about something.
Been informed or become aware of something.
Discovered something by accident.
Forgotten something that was once known.

questions.explanation: Hear of significa ter ouvido falar de alguém ou algo, isto é, saber de sua existência. No contexto, poucas pessoas conhecem a ilha. A expressão não indica escuta atenta, advertência, descoberta acidental ou esquecimento de informação.

Which question below is NOT answered by the article?

options.text: Where is Pheasant Island located?
What kind of species of birds can be seen on Pheasant Island?
How many people live on Pheasant Island?
How big is Pheasant Island?
What is the weather like on Pheasant Island?

questions.explanation: O artigo informa que a ilha fica no rio Bidasoa, é desabitada, mede menos de 200 metros de comprimento e tem clima subtropical. Menciona aves migratórias, mas não identifica suas espécies; por isso, essa é a única pergunta sem resposta específica.

Why does Pheasant Island change nationality every six months?

options.text: France and Spain could not agree on who owns the island.
The island was claimed by the Basque Country after the war.
Both nations signed a rotating tourism agreement.
France and Spain agreed to share control of the island as a symbol of peace.
It is required by European Union law.

questions.explanation: O texto associa o revezamento entre França e Espanha ao acordo de paz e ao compartilhamento do governo da ilha. Não descreve disputa territorial pendente, reivindicação basca, contrato turístico nem obrigação imposta por legislação da União Europeia.

Analyze the statements below about the text and mark T, if true, or F, if false. ( ) A monolith on the island has inscriptions in both French and Spanish. ( ) The Treaty of the Pyrenees was signed 30 years after the Franco-Spanish war ended. ( ) The island is part of the official Camino de Santiago pilgrimage route. ( ) Not many people have heard about the island that periodically changes its nationality. The correct order of filling in the parentheses, from top to bottom, is:

options.text: F – T – T – F.
T – F – T – F.
T – F – F – T.
F – F – T – T.
F – T – F – F.

questions.explanation: O monólito tem inscrições nos dois idiomas, e o texto afirma que pouca gente conhece a ilha. O tratado encerrou a guerra de trinta anos, não ocorreu trinta anos depois dela; o Caminho de Santiago é próximo, mas a ilha não integra sua rota oficial.

Mark the INCORRECT statement about Pheasant Island.

options.text: A monolith was built at the time of the Treaty of the Pyrenees signing.
A wedding was celebrated there.
There is a formal ceremony every time it changes its nationality.
Tourists are allowed on the island on specific occasions.
In December, the island belongs to France.

questions.explanation: O tratado foi assinado em 1659, enquanto o monólito foi erguido séculos depois para recordar o encontro; daí a incorreção. O texto confirma o casamento real, as cerimônias de transferência, visitas ocasionais e a administração francesa em dezembro.
